passage:
[Figure 1]

Researchers Lan Vo and Zaid Kaplan asked 312 schoolchildren in Australia to name plants they could identify in a local park. The researchers suggest that the children may be more familiar with flowering plants than with other plants in their environments.
prompt: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the researchers' conclusion?

choices.A: There were about as many lists with an example of a moss as there were with an example of a fern.
choices.B: The fewest number of lists contained an example of a fern.
choices.C: More of the lists had an example of a moss than an example of a flowering plant.
choices.D: More of the lists had an example of a flowering plant than either an example of a fern or an example of a moss.

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it accurately describes data from the graph that support the researchers' conclusion that children may be more familiar with flowering plants than with other plants. The graph shows that approximately 78% of the lists contained an example of a flowering plant, while only about 64% contained an example of a fern and only about 52% contained an example of a moss. The fact that flowering plants were included in more lists than either ferns or mosses supports the idea that children may be particularly familiar with flowering plants in their environments.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because the graph shows that more lists had an example of a flowering plant than an example of a moss, not the other way around (approximately 78% of the lists included an example of a flowering plant, while only about 52% included an example of a moss). Further, examples of a nonflowering group appearing in more lists than examples of flowering plants did would actually weaken the claim that schoolchildren may be more familiar with flowering plants than with other plants.
